terms.gloss: a raised stone edge: a quay
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.97: ad omnīs crepīdinēs urbis
terms.comment: Properly a base or raised edge; of a harbour town, its quays, as Cicero says of Syracuse. Morgan–Owens adds maris or flūminis where needed.

phrases.english: Don’t go near the edge of the quay.

phrases.latin: Forte ratis celsī conjūncta crepīdine saxī expositīs stābat scālīs et ponte parātō
phrases.english: as it happened, a ship lay moored to the ledge of a high rock, with its ladders out and its gangway ready

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. dock, quay.
